subs.text: Book fourteen.
The Loyal Swineherd.
Scene one.
The Dogs at Eumaeus's Yard.
Smoke, and the smell of pigs.
Someone keeps this hill better than the palace keeps itself.
Out of the yard four dogs came at him like wolves, and the man dropped his staff and sat down in the dirt,
old soldier's craft, letting their fury break over a harmless thing.
Back!
Off him, you brutes, off!
Old man, another moment and you'd have been torn, and the shame of it mine forever.
Sit, grandfather, here, my own seat by the fire.
Two young pigs I'll dress for us;
eat first, and tell your griefs after.

scenes.world: A remote stone-walled pig farm on a bare upland at cold dusk, rough sties and a thatched hut, wind and low cloud.

captain.asks: Let the milieu speak first: walls, sties, hut, a small beggar at the gate; then the dogs' attack and the herdsman's rescue inside that farm.
diagnosis: The farm is a 20th-century dairy: clapboard houses, sheep, cows, fences; the pigs only arrive in the last shot.
Dogs run and a man herds them, so action reads, but the beggar who is attacked never appears.
Upland bw texture is consistent; a stranger follows 'farm, dogs, kindly man, food' without knowing who is threatened.

scenes.title: The Swineherd Laments His Master
scenes.card: The swineherd curses the suitors eating his master's herds; the beggar swears Odysseus will return, but Eumaeus will not believe it.

subs.text: Scene two.
The Swineherd Laments His Master.
Forgive the poor meat, old man;
young pork is all the suitors leave us.
The fattened boars go down the mountain to men who eat a lost king's herds and fear no god watching.
My master, and I will say his name, Odysseus, was kind to me past any telling, and the sea has him now,
dead in some far water.
Every drifter who wants supper sings me a tale that he lives.
I have stopped believing songs.
Then hear an oath, not a song.
By Zeus of guests, by this table and this fire:
Odysseus comes home before this year is out.
When he stands in his own hall, give me a cloak and tunic then, and not one hour before.
Keep your oath, friend, for I'll pay no cloak on it, and Odysseus will not come.
Drink your wine and speak of other things;
my heart aches enough whenever his name is said.

scenes.world: A smoky thatched hut on a cold upland pig farm at night, firelight on rough timber and stone, plain wooden bowls.

captain.asks: Hold the two at the meal in one static, long-held quotidian frame by the fire, without cutting on the lines.
diagnosis: The sign wants one held two-shot; the cut is eight strangers in eight rooms, the opposite of static.
After steering, the dark hut with two figures by a pot recurs and gives the scene a home; NOW had a 1950s living room.
Colour cattle, modern dinners and a US flag tempt every row; the quotidian slides toward the advertising page.

scenes.title: The Cretan Tale at the Hut
scenes.card: The disguised king tells a long invented life story, testing how much the swineherd will believe.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Cretan Tale at the Hut.
But you now, who are you, and from where among men?
What ship brought you, and what grief?
For no man walks to Ithaca.
Crete, then Troy, then Egypt in chains, go on, leave nothing out.
And this Thesprotian king, say again what he swore to you about Odysseus and the treasure coming home.
Mark how he builds it:
true harbors, true wars, true hunger, and a false name at the keel.
The lie is a net, cast gently, to sound the depth of the swineherd's heart.
Poor man, your wanderings wring my heart, and every word of hardship I believe.
But the word about Odysseus, no.
Why do you good men think a lie will comfort me?

scenes.title: The Cloak Test
scenes.card: On a cold night, the beggar hints with a story that he needs a cloak, and the swineherd generously lends one.

subs.text: Scene four.
The Cloak Test.
Night turns cold and wet as Eumaeus's herdsmen return.
Hear a boast from an old soldier, since wine loosens me.
One freezing ambush-night at Troy I lay without a cloak,
and Odysseus spun a trick on the spot that got one onto my shoulders.
Ah, to be that young man tonight, someone in this hut might do the same.
Well hinted, old man, and no fault in the hint.
Here, my spare cloak, sleep warm.
Eumaeus sleeps near the pigs himself, guarding the herd through the storm.

sign.name: Theatrical figure
sign.operation: Hold the teller; cut to the cloak.

scenes.world: A rough upland hut and pig yard on a cold storm-lashed night, rain sheeting past firelit doorway, wind in the thatch.

captain.asks: Hold the teller as a theatrical figure performing his boast, then cut to the cloak it earns, inside a storm-lashed night.
diagnosis: The teller finally exists: a bald, wild-browed old man speaks to camera; the scene has its actor.
The cloak never appears as a cloak: pelts, shawls and draped women stand in, so the payoff is implied.
Storm reads as murk rather than rain; snow-and-colour pigs tempt every row and must be refused.

prologue: Disguised as a beggar, Odysseus reaches the farm of his old swineherd. Before trusting anyone, he must learn who is still loyal to him.

cast.name: The suitors

carry: The swineherd is truly loyal, though he refuses to believe his master will ever come home.
